A.explanation: Combined regime: the national framework (2023 marker and surgery ban, extremism designation, propaganda law, 101 extremism convictions, club raids, a death in pretrial custody) is the operative floor. The occupied city adds a layer on top: no local mitigation, UN-documented sexual-violence risk in occupation detention, unofficial detention sites with torture, and restricted movement with document checks. Visitors without the occupying state's passport face checkpoint scrutiny and possible statelessness treatment. No remedy operates locally. This sits below the parent regime, not at it.

entry_documents.exposure: Home-issued documents remain unaltered; no marker change or surgery route. Checkpoint and document checks are pervasive in the naval city, and non-occupying-state passport holders are treated as stateless with severely restricted movement.
entry_documents.interaction: A mismatch at a checkpoint can escalate into detention under occupation authority, where civilians are held without lawyers or family access.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Occupation authorities detain civilians in unofficial sites with documented torture and ill-treatment; UN reporting finds LGBTQ+ persons at acute risk of sexual violence. A national-level death in pretrial custody on extremism charges is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No lawyer or family access in occupation sites; no protective custody documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention on extremism or document grounds routes a visitor directly into the documented torture and sexual-violence pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The city is administered as a federal city of the occupying state, so the full federal regime applies: all-audiences propaganda law, 2023 ban on gender-affirming care and legal recognition, and extremist designation with up to twelve years for participation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal rules are enforced through local occupation institutions with no independent layer, so the harshest federal rule governs.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care is banned under the 2023 federal law; no local provision is documented.
care_services.interaction: A medical need arising during detention or checkpoint delay cannot be met through a local route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The state designates the LGBT movement extremist; police raid venues, photograph patrons and bring extremism charges. Official framing treats trans identity as a threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement against venues and symbols reaches visitors through the same federal channel, with occupation authorities as the operator.

minors_guardians.exposure: Propaganda law bars material giving minors a desire to change sex; the 2023 gender-transition law and 2024 adoption ban affect families. A minor's presence with a trans adult creates exposure to the same enforcement.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian's documents or a minor's care can invite inquiry under the propaganda and transition rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police-led venue raids and occupation predation are documented; the occupied peninsula's threats apply in the city.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No local protective institution, monitor or remedy operates.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are the threat source, so reporting an assault is unlikely to lead to protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No independent monitor, local remedy or hate-crime recording. Official non-recording of anti-LGBT hate crime is documented at national level.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Foreign safe-haven calls and asylum framing exist but are not traveller-facing protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The lack of recourse compounds the detention exposure; unknown treatment of visitors in unofficial sites is a serious open question.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: arrest for presentation, custody beatings, unavailable remedies and no capital application. A is similar in custody and remedy failure, but adds documented death in detention and UN-reported sexual-violence risk. Lower than or similar to 0.15-A because the occupation layer is harsher than a formal capital-free regime.

Housing by birth sex and raids on support centres mirror A's enforced exposures, but 0.25-C has no documented custodial death, no extremism designation and no occupation detention. A is clearly below 0.25-C.

0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention with compensation and tribunal appeals. A has none of these operative protections, so A sits far below. Reaching 0.75 would require lawful recognition, enforced anti-discrimination and an end to extremism-based arrests.

A.synthesis: The national extremism and propaganda regime is enforced through venue raids, convictions and custodial deaths, with no marker or care route. The occupied city imports the full federal regime and adds occupation detention, documented torture and sexual-violence risk, and statelessness-based movement restrictions, with no local remedy. Documented custody lethality plus universal document checks makes imprisonment and serious harm highly plausible after discovery, placing A at the severe end, below the national baseline.

B.explanation: Combined regime: the national framework alone applies, as the division has no documented sub-national signal. It bans gender-marker change and gender-affirming care, criminalises propaganda and extremism participation (2-6 years, organising 6-10 years), and enforces through venue raids and convictions, with a documented death in pretrial custody. No sub-national mitigation is documented, but absence of sub-national material is unresolved rather than safe. Same-sex conduct is not criminalised, which is a secondary signal only. This places B in the severe band, above A because no occupation-detention layer is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Home-issued passports and visas remain as issued; marker change and surgery are banned, so visitors cannot align documents. Mismatches can prompt questioning under the extremism regime.
entry_documents.interaction: A document mismatch at entry or in hotel checks can lead to investigation, which routes into the extremism and propaganda framework.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Extremism charges have been brought over an LGBT travel business and a detainee died in pretrial custody (Dec 2024); 20 criminal charges and 81 administrative guilty findings for symbols are documented nationally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention on extremism grounds is the national pathway; the sub-national custody picture is unresolved.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National propaganda and extremism statutes apply; the 2023 transition ban voids same-sex marriage involving trans persons.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No sub-national decree or divergence documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The national regime governs without local modification; the absence of sub-national material is not evidence of local safety.

care_services.exposure: Trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023 at national level.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing ongoing care has no documented local route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Top-court designation of the LGBT movement as extremist and ongoing enforcement frame trans and LGBT visibility as a security matter.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement against symbols and venues reaches visitors through the national channel.

minors_guardians.exposure: Propaganda law covers material giving minors a desire to change sex; the 2024 adoption ban on citizens of transition-permitting countries affects families. A minor travelling with a trans adult carries inquiry exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Documents or care for a minor can attract scrutiny under the national statutes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Public hostility is documented (74% say homosexuality should not be accepted); the national government does not record anti-LGBT hate crimes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime aggravation or sub-national protection documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims lack a recording or recourse channel, so street harm is unlikely to be remedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No sub-national monitoring, remedy or complaint record was located; this absence is unresolved, not reassuring.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Asylum framing and foreign safe-haven calls exist but are not traveller-facing protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown local practice combined with the national regime leaves the exposure unbounded below.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A is a visitor-specific register exclusion with no arrest and an appeal path. B has documented national prosecutions for participation, custodial death and no appeal, so B sits below 0.35-A.

0.25-D has selective police entrapment, fines and short jail terms, with some appellate annulments. B shares the national statutes and documented custodial death, with no appellate remedy documented. B is similar to or below 0.25-D.

0.75-C has trained border officers, compensated unlawful holding and tribunal appeals. B lacks all of these, so it sits far below. Reaching 0.75 would require repeal of the extremism and propaganda statutes and an operative anti-discrimination regime.

B.synthesis: The national extremism and propaganda regime applies in full, with convictions, venue raids and a custodial death documented, and no marker or care route. No sub-national mitigation is documented, and the absence of local material is unresolved rather than safe. Universal document exposure at entry plus enforcement through the extremism framework make serious consequences after discovery plausible, but no occupation-detention or torture layer is documented, so B sits above A and in the severe band.
